business_problem: bp needs safer, faster, data-informed operations across oil and gas, retail, and facilities while handling data volumes that specialists cannot review manually, including seismic datasets, well design options, and operational status across thousands of fuel and industrial assets.
solution_summary: bp is deploying AI across operational workflows rather than as a single application. The company is building a unified data platform with Databricks and Palantir so essential statistical and operational data from assets around the world can be made accessible wherever it is needed inside bp. On top of that foundation, teams use generative AI through Palantir's Foundry and Microsoft copilot to support daily work, search internal operational questions, and interpret patterns in equipment and performance data. In field operations, AI helps engineers evaluate hundreds of well trajectories in less than a day instead of taking weeks or months. bp also describes using the same data-and-AI approach to monitor fuel pumps and gas compressors, predict when equipment is about to go offline, and initiate actions to keep assets running. The wider architecture is cloud-first, with most corporate data already in the cloud and expanded HPC capacity supporting compute-heavy workloads such as seismic imaging.

data_flow: Operational and statistical data from bp assets, gas stations, facilities, and subsurface workflows is brought into a unified data platform built with Databricks and Palantir. Employees query that shared foundation through Palantir's Foundry and Microsoft copilot, and AI analyzes patterns in the data to return operational answers or predictions such as impending equipment outages so teams can act.
